title: The Downbeat Split
primary_metric: rehearsal minutes required per second of timing accuracy gained

options.A: The Straight Cut — ship the already-rehearsed straight-subdivision arrangement and absorb the timing gap with a small tempo compromise
options.B: The Downbeat Split — rewrite the beat with a syncopated subdivision that hits the target duration exactly, at the cost of additional rehearsal time

_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC §4
protagonist: Elena Cross, staff arranger, Larkspur Sound
concept_sheet: The Downbeat Split — approved concept, provided directly by user 2026-08-24 (not from a CONCEPTS_*.md file)

deliverables.text: The Straight Cut's computed total running time: mixed-number beat length x mixed-number seconds-per-beat, multiplied across every phrase repeat, with full arithmetic shown.
A partial-phrase check: a fractional portion of the final phrase's mixed-number beat length, multiplied out to locate the target cutoff inside the running time.
The Downbeat Split's beat-subdivision calculation: the fractional timing gap divided by the ensemble's fractional subdivision unit, with full arithmetic shown.
A rehearsal read-through fit-check: mixed-number rehearsal time remaining divided by the length of one read-through of the syncopated passage.

A final decision table: rehearsal minutes required (mixed-number minutes-per-read-through x whole-number read-throughs), timing accuracy in seconds, and rehearsal minutes per second of timing accuracy gained, for both options, with a stated recommendation.

balance.argument_a: The Straight Cut books zero additional rehearsal minutes -- the ensemble already sight-reads it cleanly -- and absorbs the remaining timing gap with a small, uniform tempo nudge across the whole cue. Against the primary metric, its rehearsal-minute numerator is at or near zero, so its ratio looks unbeatable on the page.
balance.argument_b: The Downbeat Split is the only version that lands on the broadcast slot's target exactly, not approximately. Its rehearsal cost is small, bounded, and one-time: a fixed number of read-throughs at the AFM's real published rehearsal rate, paid once, in exchange for a take that clears the network's frame-accuracy tolerance for the life of the ad buy.
balance.margin_basis: Once Appendices A-D are sourced or their Modeling Assumptions are accepted, compute rehearsal minutes required per second of timing accuracy gained for both options (D5) and compare directly. Because Option A's rehearsal-minute numerator is likely at or near zero, the comparison turns on how the case frames Option A's real cost (risk of a take that misses the network's frame-accuracy tolerance) rather than on a simple two-variable ratio trade-off.
